sanskrit: asayo 'tra kapālāni puroḍāśāḥ śirāṃsi ca havis tu rudhiraṃ kṛṣṇa asmin yajñe bhaviṣyati
english: The swords here are the sacrificial ladles, the oblation-cakes are the severed heads, O Kṛṣṇa, and blood shall be the clarified butter-offering in this sacrifice.

sanskrit: idhmāḥ paridhayaś caiva śaktyo 'tha vimalā gadāḥ sadasyā droṇaśiṣyāś ca kṛpasya ca śaradvataḥ
english: The firewood and enclosing sticks are the spears and bright maces, and the priests at the session are the disciples of Droṇa and of Kṛpa, son of Śaradvān.

sanskrit: iṣavo 'tra paristomā muktā gāṇḍīvadhanvanā mahārathaprayuktāś ca droṇadrauṇipracoditāḥ
english: The arrows shot by the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva bow, and those launched by great warriors and urged on by Droṇa and Aśvatthāmā, are the sacrificial straw-bundles here.

sanskrit: prātiprasthānikaṃ karma sātyakiḥ sa kariṣyati dīkṣito dhārtarāṣṭro 'tra patnī cāsya mahācamūḥ
english: Sātyaki shall perform the assistant's rite here; the consecrated sacrificer is the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and his great army serves as the sacrificial wife.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkaco 'tra śāmitraṃ kariṣyati mahābalaḥ atirātre mahābāho vitate yajñakarmaṇi
english: The mighty Ghaṭotkaca shall perform the slaughtering rite here, O great-armed one, when the sacrifice is extended into the all-night ceremony.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇā tv asya yajñasya dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ pratāpavān vaitāne karmaṇi tate jāto yaḥ kṛṣṇa pāvakāt
english: The sacrificial fee of this sacrifice is the valiant Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O Kṛṣṇa — he who was born from fire when the Vedic ritual was performed.

sanskrit: yad abruvam ahaṃ kṛṣṇa kaṭukāni sma pāṇḍavān priyārthaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya tena tapye 'dya karmaṇā
english: Whatever harsh words I spoke to the Pāṇḍavas for the sake of pleasing the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — O Kṛṣṇa, I am now burned by that deed.

sanskrit: yadā drakṣyasi māṃ kṛṣṇa nihataṃ savyasācinā punaś citis tadā cāsya yajñasyātha bhaviṣyati
english: When you shall see me slain, O Kṛṣṇa, by Savyasācin, then shall the re-piling of the altar fire of this sacrifice take place.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanasya rudhiraṃ yadā pāsyati pāṇḍavaḥ ānardaṃ nardataḥ samyak tadā sutyaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: When the Pāṇḍava drinks the blood of Duḥśāsana, roaring as he roars aloud — then shall the soma-pressing day of this sacrifice arrive.

sanskrit: yadā droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca pāñcālyau pātayiṣyataḥ tadā yajñāvasānaṃ tad bhaviṣyati janārdana
english: When the two sons of Pāñcāla shall lay low both Droṇa and Bhīṣma, that shall be the concluding rite of this sacrifice, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ yadā hantā bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ tadā samāpsyate yajño dhārtarāṣṭrasya mādhava
english: When the mighty Bhīmasena shall slay Duryodhana, then the sacrifice of the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra shall be complete, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: snuṣāś ca prasnuṣāś caiva dhṛtarāṣṭrasya saṃgatāḥ hateśvarā hatasutā hatanāthāś ca keśava
english: The daughters-in-law and granddaughters-in-law of Dhṛtarāṣṭra assembled together, their lords slain, their sons slain, their protectors slain, O Keśava —

sanskrit: gāndhāryā saha rodantyaḥ śvagṛdhrakurarākule sa yajñe 'sminn avabhṛtho bhaviṣyati janārdana
english: — weeping together with Gāndhārī amid jackals, vultures, and ospreys: that shall be the concluding bath of this sacrifice, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: vidyāvṛddhā vayovṛddhāḥ kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriyarṣabha vṛthāmṛtyuṃ na kurvīraṃs tvatkṛte madhusūdana
english: Kṣatriyas advanced in learning and advanced in age should not be caused to die in vain on your account, O bull among kshatriyas, O Madhusūdana.

sanskrit: śastreṇa nidhanaṃ gacchet samṛddhaṃ kṣatramaṇḍalam kurukṣetre puṇyatame trailokyasyāpi keśava
english: Let the full circle of the kshatriya order find death by the sword at Kurukṣetra, the holiest of all three worlds, O Keśava.

sanskrit: tad atra puṇḍarīkākṣa vidhatsva yad abhīpsitam yathā kārtsnyena vārṣṇeya kṣatraṃ svargam avāpnuyāt
english: Therefore, O lotus-eyed one, O Vārṣṇeya, arrange what you desire, so that the entire kshatriya class may attain heaven.

sanskrit: yāvat sthāsyanti girayaḥ saritaś ca janārdana tāvat kīrtibhavaḥ śabdaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: As long as the mountains and rivers shall stand, O Janārdana, so long shall this fame-born, eternal renown endure.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kathayiṣyanti mahābhāratam āhavam samāgameṣu vārṣṇeya kṣatriyāṇāṃ yaśodharam
english: Brahmins shall tell of the great Bhārata battle at their assemblies, O Vārṣṇeya — that battle which upholds the glory of the kshatriyas.

sanskrit: samupānaya kaunteyaṃ yuddhāya mama keśava mantrasaṃvaraṇaṃ kurvan nityam eva paraṃtapa
english: Bring the son of Kuntī to battle against me, O Keśava, always keeping your counsels concealed, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca karṇasya vacanaṃ śrutvā keśavaḥ paravīrahā uvāca prahasan vākyaṃ smitapūrvam idaṃ tadā
english: Sañjaya said: Having heard the words of Karṇa, Keśava, the slayer of enemy heroes, then spoke this speech laughing, beginning with a smile.

sanskrit: api tvāṃ na tapet karṇa rājyalābhopapādanā mayā dattāṃ hi pṛthivīṃ na praśāsitum icchasi
english: Does not the gaining of a kingdom burn you, O Karṇa? The earth that has been offered to you, you do not wish to rule.

sanskrit: dhruvo jayaḥ pāṇḍavānām itīdaṃ; na saṃśayaḥ kaś cana vidyate 'tra jayadhvajo dṛśyate pāṇḍavasya; samucchrito vānararāja ugraḥ
english: The victory of the Pāṇḍavas is certain — of this there is no doubt whatsoever here; the victory-banner of the Pāṇḍava is seen raised aloft, with the fierce monkey-king upon it.

sanskrit: divyā māyā vihitā bhauvanena; samucchritā indraketuprakāśā divyāni bhūtāni bhayāvahāni; dṛśyanti caivātra bhayānakāni
english: A divine illusion has been arranged by the lord of the worlds; it is raised up, blazing like Indra's banner; divine beings, terrifying and fearsome, are seen there as well.

sanskrit: na sajjate śailavanaspatibhya; ūrdhvaṃ tiryag yojanamātrarūpaḥ śrīmān dhvajaḥ karṇa dhanaṃjayasya; samucchritaḥ pāvakatulyarūpaḥ
english: It does not catch on mountains or forest trees; extending a yojana upward and across, the glorious banner of Dhanañjaya is raised up, O Karṇa, blazing like fire.

sanskrit: yadā drakṣyasi saṃgrāme śvetāśvaṃ kṛṣṇasārathim aindram astraṃ vikurvāṇam ubhe caivāgnimārute
english: When in battle you shall see the white-horsed one with Kṛṣṇa as charioteer, wielding the Aindra weapon and both the fire and wind weapons —

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvasya ca nirghoṣaṃ visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ na tadā bhavitā tretā na kṛtaṃ dvāparaṃ na ca
english: — and hear the twanging of the Gāṇḍīva bow like the crash of a thunderbolt, then there shall be neither the Tretā age nor the Kṛta nor the Dvāpara.

sanskrit: yadā drakṣyasi saṃgrāme kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram japahomasamāyuktaṃ svāṃ rakṣantaṃ mahācamūm
english: When in battle you shall see Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, engaged in muttered prayer and fire-offerings, protecting his great army —

sanskrit: ādityam iva durdharṣaṃ tapantaṃ śatruvāhinīm na tadā bhavitā tretā na kṛtaṃ dvāparaṃ na ca
english: — irresistible like the sun, scorching the enemy host, then there shall be neither the Tretā age nor the Kṛta nor the Dvāpara.

sanskrit: yadā drakṣyasi saṃgrāme bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam duḥśāsanasya rudhiraṃ pītvā nṛtyantam āhave
english: When in battle you shall see the mighty Bhīmasena drinking the blood of Duḥśāsana and dancing in the fight —

sanskrit: prabhinnam iva mātaṅgaṃ pratidviradaghātinam na tadā bhavitā tretā na kṛtaṃ dvāparaṃ na ca
english: — like a rogue elephant, a slayer of rival elephants, then there shall be neither the Tretā age nor the Kṛta nor the Dvāpara.

sanskrit: yadā drakṣyasi saṃgrāme mādrīputrau mahārathau vāhinīṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ kṣobhayantau gajāv iva
english: When in battle you shall see the two great chariot-warriors, sons of Mādrī, shaking the army of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra like two elephants —

sanskrit: vigāḍhe śastrasaṃpāte paravīrarathārujau na tadā bhavitā tretā na kṛtaṃ dvāparaṃ na ca
english: — plunging into the thick of weapons, smashing the chariots of enemy heroes, then there shall be neither the Tretā age nor the Kṛta nor the Dvāpara.

sanskrit: yadā drakṣyasi saṃgrāme droṇaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ kṛpam suyodhanaṃ ca rājānaṃ saindhavaṃ ca jayadratham
english: When in battle you shall see Droṇa, Śāntanava Bhīṣma, Kṛpa, King Suyodhana, and Jayadratha the Sindhu king —

sanskrit: yuddhāyāpatatas tūrṇaṃ vāritān savyasācinā na tadā bhavitā tretā na kṛtaṃ dvāparaṃ na ca
english: — rushing swiftly into combat, held at bay by Savyasācin, then there shall be neither the Tretā age nor the Kṛta nor the Dvāpara.

sanskrit: brūyāḥ karṇa ito gatvā droṇaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ kṛpam saumyo 'yaṃ vartate māsaḥ suprāpayavasendhanaḥ
english: Go from here, O Karṇa, and tell Droṇa, Śāntanava, and Kṛpa: 'This mild month is at hand, well-supplied with barley, food, and fuel.'

sanskrit: pakvauṣadhivanasphītaḥ phalavān alpamakṣikaḥ niṣpaṅko rasavat toyo nātyuṣṇaśiśiraḥ sukhaḥ
english: 'The forests of ripened herbs are full, there is fruit, few insects; the water is free of mud and full of flavor; the weather is neither too hot nor too cold — it is pleasant.'

sanskrit: saptamāc cāpi divasād amāvāsyā bhaviṣyati saṃgrāmaṃ yojayet tatra tāṃ hy āhuḥ śakradevatām
english: 'From the seventh day, the new moon will come — let battle be joined then; they say that day is under the lordship of Indra.'

sanskrit: tathā rājño vadeḥ sarvān ye yuddhāyābhyupāgatāḥ yad vo manīṣitaṃ tad vai sarvaṃ saṃpādayāmi vaḥ
english: 'Also tell the king and all those who have come ready for war: whatever you have wished for, I shall accomplish all of it for you.'

sanskrit: rājāno rājaputrāś ca duryodhanavaśānugāḥ prāpya śastreṇa nidhanaṃ prāpsyanti gatim uttamām
english: Kings and princes who follow Duryodhana's command, attaining death by the sword, shall reach the highest state.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca keśavasya tu tad vākyaṃ karṇaḥ śrutvā hitaṃ śubham abravīd abhisaṃpūjya kṛṣṇaṃ madhuniṣūdanam jānan māṃ kiṃ mahābāho saṃmohayitum icchasi
english: Sañjaya said: Having heard that beneficial and auspicious speech of Keśava, Karṇa, honoring Kṛṣṇa the slayer of Madhu, said: 'Knowing me as you do, O great-armed one, why do you wish to bewilder me?'

sanskrit: yo 'yaṃ pṛthivyāḥ kārtsnyena vināśaḥ samupasthitaḥ nimittaṃ tatra śakunir ahaṃ duḥśāsanas tathā duryodhanaś ca nṛpatir dhṛtarāṣṭrasuto 'bhavat
english: 'This destruction of the whole earth that has now come upon us — the occasions for it were Śakuni, myself, Duḥśāsana, and King Duryodhana, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.'

sanskrit: asaṃśayam idaṃ kṛṣṇa mahad yuddham upasthitam pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca ghoraṃ rudhirakardamam
english: 'Without doubt, O Kṛṣṇa, this great battle is at hand between the Pāṇḍavas and the Kurus — terrible, a mire of blood.'

sanskrit: rājāno rājaputrāś ca duryodhanavaśānugāḥ raṇe śastrāgninā dagdhāḥ prāpsyanti yamasādanam
english: 'Kings and princes who follow Duryodhana's command, consumed by the fire of weapons in battle, shall reach the abode of Yama.'

sanskrit: svapnā hi bahavo ghorā dṛśyante madhusūdana nimittāni ca ghorāṇi tathotpātāḥ sudāruṇāḥ
english: 'For many dreadful dreams are seen, O Madhusūdana, and dreadful omens, and fearful portents too.'

sanskrit: parājayaṃ dhārtarāṣṭre vijayaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhire śaṃsanta iva vārṣṇeya vividhā lomaharṣaṇāḥ
english: 'Various hair-raising signs seem to proclaim defeat for the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and victory for Yudhiṣṭhira, O Vārṣṇeya.'

sanskrit: prājāpatyaṃ hi nakṣatraṃ grahas tīkṣṇo mahādyutiḥ śanaiścaraḥ pīḍayati pīḍayan prāṇino 'dhikam
english: 'For the fierce planet of great brilliance, Saturn, afflicts the constellation of Prajāpati, oppressing living beings exceedingly.'

sanskrit: kṛtvā cāṅgārako vakraṃ jyeṣṭhāyāṃ madhusūdana anurādhāṃ prārthayate maitraṃ saṃśamayann iva
english: 'And Mars, having turned retrograde in Jyeshtha, O Madhusūdana, moves toward Anuradha, as though appeasing Mitra.'

sanskrit: nūnaṃ mahad bhayaṃ kṛṣṇa kurūṇāṃ samupasthitam viśeṣeṇa hi vārṣṇeya citrāṃ pīḍayate grahaḥ
english: 'Surely a great terror has come upon the Kurus, O Kṛṣṇa; for particularly, O Vārṣṇeya, a planet afflicts the star Chitra.'

sanskrit: somasya lakṣma vyāvṛttaṃ rāhur arkam upeṣyati divaś colkāḥ patanty etāḥ sanirghātāḥ sakampanāḥ
english: 'The mark of the moon has shifted; Rāhu will approach the sun; and from the sky these meteors fall with thunderclaps and tremors.'

sanskrit: niṣṭananti ca mātaṅgā muñcanty aśrūṇi vājinaḥ pānīyaṃ yavasaṃ cāpi nābhinandanti mādhava
english: 'Elephants groan and horses shed tears; they do not take joy even in water and barley, O Mādhava.'

sanskrit: prādurbhūteṣu caiteṣu bhayam āhur upasthitam nimitteṣu mahābāho dāruṇaṃ prāṇināśanam
english: 'When these omens appear, they say that a dreadful peril is at hand, O great-armed one — a destruction of living beings.'

sanskrit: alpe bhukte purīṣaṃ ca prabhūtam iha dṛśyate vājināṃ vāraṇānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca keśava
english: 'Even with little eaten, abundant excrement is seen here from horses, from elephants, and from men, O Keśava.'

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainyeṣu sarveṣu madhusūdana parābhavasya tal liṅgam iti prāhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: 'In all the armies of the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Madhusūdana — the wise declare that to be a sign of defeat.'

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭaṃ vāhanaṃ kṛṣṇa pāṇḍavānāṃ pracakṣate pradakṣiṇā mṛgāś caiva tat teṣāṃ jayalakṣaṇam
english: 'The mounts of the Pāṇḍavas are described as joyful, O Kṛṣṇa, and deer circle them clockwise — that is the sign of victory for them.'

sanskrit: apasavyā mṛgāḥ sarve dhārtarāṣṭrasya keśava vācaś cāpy aśarīriṇyas tat parābhavalakṣaṇam
english: 'All the deer circle counter-clockwise around the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Keśava, and there are disembodied voices as well — that is the sign of defeat.'

sanskrit: mayūrāḥ puṣpaśakunā haṃsāḥ sārasacātakāḥ jīvaṃ jīvakasaṃghāś cāpy anugacchanti pāṇḍavān
english: 'Peacocks, flower-birds, geese, sarus cranes, chataka birds, and flocks of jivanjivaka birds follow the Pāṇḍavas.'

sanskrit: gṛdhrāḥ kākā baḍāḥ śyenā yātudhānāḥ śalāvṛkāḥ makṣikāṇāṃ ca saṃghātā anugacchanti kauravān
english: 'Vultures, crows, herons, hawks, rakshasas, jackals, and swarms of flies follow the Kauravas.'

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainyeṣu bherīṇāṃ nāsti nisvanaḥ anāhatāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ nadanti paṭahāḥ kila
english: 'In the armies of the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the war-drums make no sound; but the kettledrums of the Pāṇḍavas sound unbeaten on their own.'

sanskrit: udapānāś ca nardanti yathā govṛṣabhās tathā dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainyeṣu tat parābhavalakṣaṇam
english: 'Wells bellow like bulls in the armies of the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — that is the sign of defeat.'

sanskrit: māṃsaśoṇitavarṣaṃ ca vṛṣṭaṃ devena mādhava tathā gandharvanagaraṃ bhānumantam upasthitam saprākāraṃ saparikhaṃ savapraṃ cārutoraṇam
english: 'A rain of flesh and blood has been rained down by heaven, O Mādhava, and a celestial city of the Gandharvas has appeared near the sun — complete with ramparts, moat, altar-mound, and beautiful gateways.'

sanskrit: kṛṣṇaś ca parighas tatra bhānum āvṛtya tiṣṭhati udayāstamaye saṃdhye vedayāno mahad bhayam ekā sṛg vāśate ghoraṃ tat parābhavalakṣaṇam
english: 'A dark halo stands there encircling the sun; at the morning and evening twilight it portends great terror. A lone she-jackal howls terribly — that is the sign of defeat.'

sanskrit: kṛṣṇagrīvāś ca śakunā lambamānā bhayānakāḥ saṃdhyām abhimukhā yānti tat parābhavalakṣaṇam
english: 'Black-necked birds, hanging in a frightful manner, fly toward the twilight — that is the sign of defeat.'

sanskrit: brāhmaṇān prathamaṃ dveṣṭi gurūṃś ca madhusūdana bhṛtyān bhaktimataś cāpi tat parābhavalakṣaṇam
english: 'He first comes to hate brahmins and then his teachers, O Madhusūdana, and also servants who are devoted to him — that is the sign of defeat.'

sanskrit: pūrvā dig lohitākārā śastravarṇā ca dakṣiṇā āmapātrapratīkāśā paścimā madhusūdana
english: 'The eastern quarter has the color of blood, the southern has the color of weapons, and the western, O Madhusūdana, resembles an unripe vessel.'

sanskrit: pradīptāś ca diśaḥ sarvā dhārtarāṣṭrasya mādhava mahad bhayaṃ vedayanti tasminn utpātalakṣaṇe
english: 'And all the quarters blaze for the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Mādhava; these portent-signs proclaim great terror.'

sanskrit: sahasrapādaṃ prāsādaṃ svapnānte sma yudhiṣṭhiraḥ adhirohan mayā dṛṣṭaḥ saha bhrātṛbhir acyuta
english: 'At the end of a dream, I saw Yudhiṣṭhira ascending a thousand-pillared palace together with his brothers, O Acyuta.'

sanskrit: śvetoṣṇīṣāś ca dṛśyante sarve te śuklavāsasaḥ āsanāni ca śubhrāṇi sarveṣām upalakṣaye
english: 'All of them are seen wearing white turbans, dressed in white garments; and I observe white seats for all of them.'

sanskrit: tava cāpi mayā kṛṣṇa svapnānte rudhirāvilā āntreṇa pṛthivī dṛṣṭā parikṣiptā janārdana
english: 'And you too, O Kṛṣṇa, were seen by me at the end of a dream encircling the earth, covered in blood, with entrails, O Janārdana.'

sanskrit: asthisaṃcayam ārūḍhaś cāmitaujā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ suvarṇapātryāṃ saṃhṛṣṭo bhuktavān ghṛtapāyasam
english: 'Yudhiṣṭhira of boundless valor, having climbed a heap of bones, joyfully ate rice cooked in clarified butter from a golden vessel.'

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro mayā dṛṣṭo grasamāno vasuṃdharām tvayā dattām imāṃ vyaktaṃ bhokṣyate sa vasuṃdharām
english: 'Yudhiṣṭhira was seen by me devouring the earth — clearly he shall enjoy this earth given to him by you.'

sanskrit: uccaṃ parvatam ārūḍho bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ gadāpāṇir naravyāghro vīkṣann iva mahīm imām
english: 'Bhīma of fierce deeds, Vṛkodara, having climbed a high mountain, club in hand, tiger among men, looks over this earth as if surveying it.'

sanskrit: kṣapayiṣyati naḥ sarvān sa suvyaktaṃ mahāraṇe viditaṃ me hṛṣīkeśa yato dharmas tato jayaḥ
english: 'He will very clearly annihilate all of us in the great battle. I know this, O Hṛṣīkeśa: where dharma is, there is victory.'

sanskrit: pāṇḍuraṃ gajam ārūḍho gāṇḍīvī sa dhanaṃjayaḥ tvayā sārdhaṃ hṛṣīkeśa śriyā paramayā jvalan
english: 'That Dhanañjaya, the Gāṇḍīva-wielder, mounted on a white elephant, blazing with supreme glory together with you, O Hṛṣīkeśa —'

sanskrit: yūyaṃ sarvān vadhiṣyadhvaṃ tatra me nāsti saṃśayaḥ pārthivān samare kṛṣṇa duryodhanapurogamān
english: '— you shall all slay the kings led by Duryodhana in battle, O Kṛṣṇa. Of this I have no doubt.'

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ śuddhakeyūrakaṇṭhatrāḥ śuklamālyāmbarāvṛtāḥ
english: 'Nakula and Sahadeva and the great chariot-warrior Sātyaki, their armlets and neck-guards gleaming, clad in white garlands and white garments —'

sanskrit: adhirūḍhā naravyāghrā naravāhanam uttamam traya ete mahāmātrāḥ pāṇḍuracchatravāsasaḥ
english: '— these three tigers among men, great ministers, sheltered by white parasols and white garments, were mounted on the finest human vehicle.'

sanskrit: śvetoṣṇīṣāś ca dṛśyante traya eva janārdana dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainyeṣu tān vijānīhi keśava
english: 'And three are seen wearing white turbans in the armies of the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Janārdana — know them, O Keśava.'

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā kṛpaś caiva kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ raktoṣṇīṣāś ca dṛśyante sarve mādhava pārthivāḥ
english: 'Aśvatthāmā, Kṛpa, and Kṛtavarmā the Sātvata — and all the kings are seen wearing red turbans, O Mādhava.'

sanskrit: uṣṭrayuktaṃ samārūḍhau bhīṣmadroṇau janārdana mayā sārdhaṃ mahābāho dhārtarāṣṭreṇa cābhibho
english: 'Bhīṣma and Droṇa were seen by me mounted on a camel-drawn vehicle, O Janārdana, together with me and the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O great-armed, O resplendent one.'

sanskrit: agastyaśāstāṃ ca diśaṃ prayātāḥ sma janārdana acireṇaiva kālena prāpsyāmo yamasādanam
english: 'We were going toward the quarter governed by Agastya, O Janārdana — in no long time we shall reach the abode of Yama.'
